## Course resources

### Statistics cheat sheet

Use the [statistics cheat sheet](cheat-sheet.qmd) as a short reference for the IMS self-study and the quiz.

It covers observations, variables, variable types, population and sample, contingency tables, bar plots, scatterplots, mean, histograms, median, quartiles, and box plots.

Every chart on the cheat sheet comes from a worked example, so you can see what each display shows and what it hides.

### Introduction to Modern Statistics (2e)

Free online textbook and exercises:

<https://openintrostat.github.io/ims/>

GitHub source:

<https://github.com/openintrostat/ims/>

### All Data Are Local

Open-access book from MIT Press:

<https://direct.mit.edu/books/oa-monograph/4323/All-Data-Are-LocalThinking-Critically-in-a-Data>

## Optional learning resources

### MaDaLi² — Mannheim Data Literacy

Bilingual German and English self-study material. No prior knowledge is required. Useful modules include data ethics, data collection, data management, analysis, interpretation, and publication.

<https://www.uni-mannheim.de/en/about/teaching/teaching-projects/data-literacy/e-learning-course-mannheim-data-literacy-madali2/>

### Data Carpentry — Social Sciences

Practical lessons on spreadsheet structure, data cleaning with OpenRefine, and data analysis workflows.

<https://datacarpentry.org/lessons/>

### Seeing Theory

Interactive visual explanations of probability and statistics. Use it for intuition and optional review.

<https://seeing-theory.brown.edu/>

## Data protection

### Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC)

Official legal information on Swiss data protection:

<https://www.edoeb.admin.ch/en/legal-basis-data-protection>

Before you use personal data, check two things. Check whether the data contain information about identifiable people. Check whether your planned use is lawful and appropriate.
